FAST

BANGKOK, Oct 16 : The head of the IMF on Friday appealed to global leaders to cooperate in the face of multiple economic risks, including rapid advances in AI and a prolonged war in the Middle East, as Washington hailed what it sees as US-led economic momentum. Their contrasting views echoed throughout this year's annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Bangkok, as finance officials and central bankers from around the world took stock of a global economy rocked by high inflation and rising interest rates that have kept growth sluggish and increased inequality. The IMF on Tuesday slightly raised its global growth forecast to 3.1 per cent in 2026, well below the historical average, as it flagged significant growth and financial stability risks from a potential ending of the AI investment boom, growing debt levels and the ongoing Middle East conflict. Absent the US-Israeli-led war against Iran and Tehran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz that triggered a massive global energy shock, the IMF has said it would have expected AI to have fueled much stronger growth.

On Friday, IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva said the sheer speed of technological change added to the long list of challenges, including disruptions to the global trading system, high food and energy prices and lingering wars, all of which threatened to widen the gulf between advanced economies and the world's poor. Bond markets, she said, were clearly sensing the risks, with US, German and Japanese 10-year sovereign yields reaching their highest levels in decades. "The need of the hour is for urgent and practical international cooperation," Georgieva, the first IMF chief from an emerging market economy, said at a plenary session on Friday. She told a subsequent panel that she spent sleepless nights worrying about how to regulate AI and ensure that poorer countries weren't left behind by its breakneck-speed development. US Treasury Under Secretary Erin Browne, in a call with reporters, pushed back against those warnings, hailing record highs on the US stock market, strong US economic output and improvements in Japan's economy. "The IMF needs to take a more balanced approach to assessing the global economic outlook," she said, adding: "The global economy has demonstrated significant resilience with strong US growth helping to support broader economic and financial stability." She said that the Fund should give equal consideration to "opportunities for positive economic shocks, particularly those driven by American innovation and super intelligence, energy abundance, and productivity-enhancing reforms." US President Donald Trump's policies on tax, trade, energy and deregulation were paving the way for stronger investment, higher productivity and durable economic growth, she said. AI JITTERS HIT STOCKS Emerging market stocks have been volatile in recent weeks, roiled by expectations of higher US interest rates that have sent borrowing costs sharply higher. Major markets have also been hit by the growing concerns over the AI investment cycle. South Korean shares posted their biggest weekly fall in 18 years as investors questioned the sustainability of the AI boom, while Japan's stock market lost 5.4 per cent over the week. Eli Remolona, governor of the Philippines' Bangko Sentral ng Pilipanas, said in an IMF panel discussion earlier in the week that he was concerned Asia had not learned the lessons of its destructive financial crisis in the late 1990s. Before the Asian financial crisis broke out in 1997, economies drew huge capital inflows that prompted the World Bank to describe it as the "East Asian miracle," Remolona said. "Investment poured into Asia, and then you had the crisis because it wasn't really a miracle. I think we have to remind ourselves about that. We have to guard against that kind of crisis," he said on Wednesday. "We have not really been making a lot of effort looking at that kind of crisis." Illustrating the vulnerability to sudden shifts, Indonesian stocks fell 11.6 per cent on Friday, their steepest one-day fall in 28 years, after global index provider MSCI said the Indonesian market was no longer worthy of "emerging market" status. Officials at the IMF and World Bank this week said they are seeing elevated demand for grant and loan programs. IMF strategy chief Christian Mummsen said the IMF's low-interest lending to low-income countries had quadrupled since the COVID pandemic, and demand was expected to remain strong. About 60 per cent of the IMF's financing since COVID had gone to low-income countries, he said.  Developing countries are increasingly outspoken about their concerns. Barbados this week joined a group of countries calling for the creation of an international panel to address inequality, citing geopolitical tensions, climate change and rapid technological advances that could further divide wealthy and poorer nations.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Thousands march in Albanian capital as anti-government protests spread
item.description: Thousands of young Albanians marched through Tirana on Friday, breaking some windows and traffic lights on the fourth day of an increasingly violent student-led campaign to force Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thousands of young Albanians marched through Tirana on Friday, breaking some windows and traffic lights on the fourth day of an increasingly violent student-led campaign to force Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign. The demonstrations, which are spreading through the country, [USN:L1N4610AQ TEXT:"turned into a riot"] in the capital on Thursday, with protesters smashing windows, raiding a bank and clashing with police. They follow months of mostly peaceful demonstrations that the students say the government ignored. "They are pushing us to the limits," said 19-year-old protester Enea, declining to give a second name for fear of arrest. He said his message to Rama was: "To resign as fast as possible before everything burns down." The students accuse officials of corruption and neglecting education and say they are angry about the sale of pristine parts of Albania's coast to a luxury resort development backed by US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner. The unrest is a challenge for Rama, who won a fourth term last year on promises to take Albania into the European Union and is aiming for membership as early as 2028. "We will not bow to violence," he said on Facebook. BUSINESSES APPEAL TO PROTESTERS TO LEAVE THEM ALONE The students, many wearing masks, faced off against lines of riot police in front of the Education Ministry building. Some small businesses had their shutters down and notes on their facades saying: "We are with you. Do not damage our business all over the town." In the coastal town of Lezha, police clashed with stone-hurling protesters. Protests have also spread to Elbasan, Skhodra and Korca, where demonstrators broke windows and set fire to garbage bins, local media reported. "We've been protesting peacefully for 140 days, and nothing was heard. So this is our only chance to be heard and get our rights that we deserve," a 19-year-old protester who gave her name only as Klea said. The demonstrations were sparked by the plans to build the resort, which has faced legal challenges. Villagers told Reuters in July that their land was wrongfully sold for development. Reuters later reported that the man who sold the land was wanted by prosecutors for drug trafficking, charges his lawyer denied. Reuters found no evidence of wrongdoing by Kushner, who is not directly involved in the villagers' dispute. Political analyst Afrim Krasniqi said younger generations saw no future in Albania. "They see that all resources in the country, political resources, economic, everything is in the hands of oligarchs," he told Reuters. Corruption scandals have tarnised Albania's image over the years and analysts say the country is a hub for gangs seeking to launder money from drugs and weapons trafficking, complicating its efforts to join the EU. Along with Montenegro, Albania is leading the accession process among Balkan countries. The unrest is part of a wave of student activism in Europe. In France, high school students [USN:L1N45Z0DG TEXT:"have staged weeks of protests"] and school blockades demanding more teachers and better facilities, arguing that deteriorating school buildings and overcrowded classrooms are undermining education.

item.title: 基調物価2％の判断、10月会合でしっかり議論 経済は見通し通り＝日銀総裁
item.description:
Takahiko Wada Takaya Yamaguchi
［１６日 ロイター］ - 日銀の植田和男総裁は１６日、基...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
基調物価2％の判断、10月会合でしっかり議論　経済は見通し通り＝日銀総裁 10/16 21:50 配信

2026年9月18日、日本銀行の政策決定会合終了後に記者会見する植田和男総裁。ロイター／キム・ギョンフン

Takahiko Wada　Takaya Yamaguchi

［１６日　ロイター］ - 日銀の植田和男総裁は１６日、基調的な物価上昇率について、２％に「かなり近づいている」と指摘する一方で、２％目標に到達したかの判断は２９日からの金融政策決定会合で「政策委員の間でしっかり議論して結論を出したい」と述べるにとどめた。

９月の決定会合以降の経済のデータは「おおむね見通し通りに動いている」とし、今回の出張で様々な当局者と意見交換をしたが、自身の見立てと「矛盾するような重要な情報がもたらされたとは考えていない」と話した。

主要２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）財務相・中央銀行総裁会議などへの出席のため訪問したタイ・バンコクで会見した。

植田総裁は基調物価が２％に迫る中、「（基調物価が）これ以上上がることは容認できず、その定着を政策の大きな目標にする」と説明した。植田総裁は９月の決定会合後の会見で「政策の局面が変化した」と言及していた。

インフレ圧力について、中東情勢と人工知能（ＡＩ）関連需要の高まりを特に注視してきたが、日銀と各国当局者の間で見解に「大きな食い違いはないとの印象を持った」と述べた。ＡＩ関連の需要動向について、日銀よりも「やや心持ちしっかりしているとみている当局者が少し多いと思った」とも話した。日銀は１０月会合で「経済・物価情勢の展望」（展望リポート）を議論する。

植田総裁は、基調物価が２％に近づき、金融環境が緩和的な中で、経済・物価・金融情勢に応じて「政策金利を引き上げて緩和度合いを調整していく」と述べた。政策調整のタイミングやペースについては、中東情勢やＡＩ関連の需要動向、為替相場の動きを見ながら、見通しの確度やリスクを点検しながら検討していくと改めて説明した。

中立金利については「はっきりとこの辺にあると申し上げられるような材料があるわけではない」とし、これまでの利上げの累積的な効果を見極めながら判断していきたいと述べた。

８月３１日から９月１日に米国・アッシュビルでＧ２０や主要７カ国（Ｇ７）の財務相・中銀総裁会議が開かれた際、植田総裁はベセント米財務長官と会談した。この日の会見では、アッシュビルでの会談以降は「コミュニケーションは特に取っていない」と述べた。ウォーシュ米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）議長とは「様々な意見交換をした」としたが、具体的な内容は明らかにしなかった。

植田総裁とともに会見に臨んだ三村淳財務官は、足もとの金融市場の状況について「今に限らず、いつにあっても常に金融市場の状況をしっかりと注視し、決しておかしなリスクが顕在化しないようにしっかりと取り組む」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：日米金融政策の転換とドル／円の行方＝植野大作氏 コラム：サービス価格上昇に加速の気配、日銀の緩和修正判断に影響も コラム：漸進的な日銀の緩和修正、ドル130円割れは短期間か＝植野大作氏 コラム：ドル／円の昨年高値更新に現実味、中立金利や介入効果に注目＝内田稔氏 コラム：食品値下げは広がるのか、日銀判断にも影響する分岐点に 最終更新: 10/16(金) 21:59 ロイター

item.title: Supermarket operator Ahold's websites, app remain offline 5 days after cyber incident
item.description: AMSTERDAM, Oct 16 : Websites and online delivery services at grocery chains belonging to Dutch supermarket operator Ahold remained offline for a fifth day on Friday following what the company has described as a "cybersecurity incident" that prompted it to shut down some of its own IT systems. An Ahold spokes
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Supermarket operator Ahold's websites, app remain offline 5 days after cyber incident

FILE PHOTO: A customer is seen inside Albert Heijn shop, operated by Ahold Delhaize, the Dutch-Belgian supermarket operator, in Eindhoven, Netherlands, January 23, 2019. REUTERS/Eva Plevier/File Photo

FAST

AMSTERDAM, Oct 16 : Websites and online delivery services at grocery chains belonging to Dutch supermarket operator Ahold remained offline for a fifth day on Friday following what the company has described as a "cybersecurity incident" that prompted it to shut down some of its own IT systems.  An Ahold spokesperson said the parent company cannot comment about the situation at its individual chains. Its US brands, which include Stop & Shop, Giant Food, Hannaford and Food Lion, are collectively one of the largest food retailers in the United States. Physical stores remain open.  Ahold's Albert Heijn chain, the Netherlands' largest, has been gradually recovering from the shutdown that began October 11, disrupting its distribution centres and leading to empty produce shelves. Albert Heijn does not expect online delivery to resume before Sunday. The Netherlands' Justice Minister David van Weel called on the company on Friday to file a criminal complaint over the incident, which Ahold has avoided describing as a hack, saying in a statement that no "customer, associate and partner data was taken".

"I understand that in the heat of the moment, a company like this is concerned with preventing damage to its systems and is not immediately looking outward," the minister told Dutch press agency ANP. "I think that we're in calmer waters now and the time has come to take this step." The Ahold spokesperson said the company could not respond to the politician's remarks and pointed to its most recent statement on October 14, in which it said the company was working with relevant internal teams and external cybersecurity experts and engaging with the appropriate authorities and other stakeholders as necessary. That statement said that because Ahold's investigation is ongoing, it could not share details about what happened in order not to undermine its own security or interfere with its response.

Source: Reuters

item.title: ロシア無人機、ウクライナ各地攻撃 3人死亡
item.description: [キーウ（キエフ） １６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[キーウ（キエフ） １６日 ロイター] - ウクライナ当局によると、１６日未明に各地でロシアの無人機（ドローン）攻撃があり、少なくとも３人が死亡した。商業施設２カ所が攻撃を受けたほか、北西部では電力網への攻撃で約３７万人が停電の影響を受けた。

ハルキウ州知事によると、東部ハルキウ市の３地区への攻撃で２人が死亡、１２人が負傷した。同氏は当初、死者を３人としていた。

ポーランドと国境を接する北西部ヴォルィーニ 州では、食品加工施設への攻撃で１人が死亡、８人が負傷した。

当局によると、前線に近い北部スムイ市と、ヴォルィーニ州に隣接するリウネ州でも、それぞれ少なくとも１カ所の商業施設が攻撃を受けた。

item.title: US import prices increase; post largest annual gain in more than four years
item.description: US import prices increased more than expected in September, boosted by higher costs for energy products and a range of other goods, further evidence of rising inflation pressures as the Middle East conflict persists.
item.dc:creator: Lucia Mutikani
item.content:encoded: US import prices increased more than expected in September, boosted by higher costs for energy products and a range of other goods, further evidence of rising inflation pressures as the Middle East conflict persists. The report from the Labor Department on Friday followed data this week showing strong increases in [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"consumer"] and [USN:L1N460127 TEXT:"producer"] prices last month, which left economists convinced that inflation was broadening beyond the energy sector. The drawn-out US-Israeli war with Iran has snarled supply chains, and is keeping oil prices elevated. Economists have attributed rising inflation to President Donald Trump's policies, including tariffs on imports and the Middle East conflict. A Reuters/Ipsos poll also showed about 78% of Americans [USN:L6N45T0W3 TEXT:"blamed Trump's"] policies for the rising cost of living. "Americans face an inflation threat literally on every front and everywhere they turn they have to reach in their pocketbooks and pay a little bit more for the same goods that were cheaper just a few months ago," said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS. "There was no import goods inflation before Trump 2.0 economic policies started to roll out in January 2025, but this year it is everywhere." Import prices jumped 1.1% last month after rebounding by a downwardly revised 0.5% in August, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast import prices, which exclude tariffs, increasing 0.8% after a previously reported 0.7% advance in August. In the 12 months through September, import prices rose 8.1%, the largest gain since July 2022, after increasing 6.7% in August. Despite inflation heating up in September, financial markets still expected the Federal Reserve to skip raising interest rates later this month and tighten monetary policy in December. The US central bank in September raised its [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"overnight benchmark interest rate"] by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range. Fed Chairman [USN:S0N40K04F TEXT:"Kevin Warsh,"] speaking in Bangkok, Thailand, on Friday gave no preview about whether he feels more interest-rate hikes will be needed, or when, in keeping with his style since taking the reins as central bank chief in May. Stocks on Wall Street were mixed. The dollar fell against a basket of currencies. US Treasury yields fell. Imported fuel prices rebounded 4.8% last month after falling 0.2% in August. Food prices were unchanged after dropping 0.6% in August. Excluding food and fuels, import prices advanced 0.7%, matching the prior month's increase. The so-called core import prices rose 6.2% in the 12 months through September. Capital goods prices increased 0.9% after rising by the same margin in August, boosted by prices for computers, peripherals and semiconductors amid an AI investment boom. There was also a rise in the cost of imported industrial and service machinery, which more than offset a decline in the prices of scientific and medical machinery. ACCELERATION IN INFLATION ANTICIPATED Prices for imported consumer goods, excluding automotives, increased 0.4%, driven by a 0.7% surge in the cost of long-lasting manufactured goods. The cost of imported automotive vehicles, parts and engines increased 0.3%. Prices of imports from China increased 0.7%, the most since December 2021. Prices gained 3.1% in the 12 months through September. There were also increases in the prices of imports from Japan, the European Union, Mexico and Canada. The report also showed a 12.6% surge in import air passenger fares last month after declining in July and August. Economists said the international airfares component that goes into the calculation of the Personal Consumption Expenditures price indexes, the inflation measures tracked by the Federal Reserve for its 2% target, was unchanged after they adjusted the data for seasonal fluctuations. Economists' estimates for the increase in September's core PCE price index were little changed in the 0.31% to 0.36% range, which could round up to 0.4%. That would translate to a year-over-year rise of 3.1%. Core PCE inflation gained 0.2% in August and advanced 3.0% on a year-over-year basis. "We're looking for inflation to accelerate in the near term but not plateau at a higher level," said Oren Klachkin, financial markets economist at Nationwide. "That said, the risk is inflation remains higher for longer than we expect and is more difficult for the Fed to vanquish." Though the AI investment spree is contributing to fueling inflation, it is also underpinning manufacturing. A separate report from the Fed showed [USN:L1N46110A TEXT:"factory production"] rebounded 0.3% in September, also supported by businesses replenishing inventories to meet robust domestic demand. Output fell 0.2% in August. It advanced 1.1% on a year-over-year basis in September. But factory production lost significant momentum in the third quarter, growing at a 0.7% annualized rate after accelerating at a 5.6% pace in the April-June quarter. Manufacturing accounts for about 9.4% of the economy. Output of semiconductors and related electronic components surged 28.4% last quarter, which some economists shrugged off. Motor vehicle and parts production fell 3.0% in September and contracted at a 3.4% rate last quarter. "While strong AI-demand has boosted business investment, much of this investment is imported, implying domestic production has not been as strong," said Veronica Clark, an economist at Citigroup. Outside AI-supporting industries, downside risks to production are mounting from elevated energy prices, a trade war with Canada, rising borrowing costs and fading stimulus from tax incentives. Record high diesel prices could soon raise the cost of goods, including at the supermarket, weighing on demand. Capacity utilization for the manufacturing sector edged up to 75.9% from 75.8% in August. It is 2.3 percentage points below its long-run average. "This means producers may be inclined to absorb some of the increase in energy and other input costs, but clearly not all, as suggested by this week's heated consumer and producer price reports," said Sal Guatieri, a senior economist at BMO Capital Markets.

item.title: Hedge funds bet Japan reforms have further to run at Sohn Tokyo
item.description: The next phase of Japanese corporate reform took center stage at the Sohn Conference in Tokyo, as hedge fund managers highlighted investment opportunities ranging from a financial conglomerate's capital allocation strategy to an X-ray scattering firm's AI solutions.
item.dc:creator: Summer Zhen, Rocky Swift
item.content:encoded: The next phase of Japanese corporate reform took center stage at the Sohn Conference in Tokyo, as hedge fund managers highlighted investment opportunities ranging from a financial conglomerate's capital allocation strategy to an X-ray scattering firm's AI solutions. At the inaugural Sohn Conference in Japan, which invited 14 funds to pitch their top investment ideas, more than half of the investors favored the theme of corporate reform. Daisuke Nakayama, a portfolio manager at Hong Kong-headquartered Polymer Capital, picked Orix Corporation , a financial services firm, saying the change in management marks "a big turning point" for the company's transformation into a global investment firm. "The new leadership has a greater focus on capital allocation and ROE," Nakayama said, adding the firm is now using overseas capital, including from Qatar Investment Authority, to bid for companies. The number of activist campaigns in Japan hit a record last year, according to brokerage Jefferies, after years of pressure from regulators and the Tokyo Stock Exchange on companies to improve shareholder returns and invest in growth. BEYOND DIVIDENDS AND BUYBACKS Fund managers said that the next chapter is not just about companies increasing dividends and buybacks but also about focusing on those deploying capital to expand businesses and drive long-term growth. One example is Rigaku (268A.T) , an X-ray equipment supplier pivoting to semiconductor metrology, measuring and inspecting chips. New York-based Indus Capital Partners said it had invested in the company and had engaged with the firm to sell a stake to a US semiconductor firm to drive revenue. As semiconductor companies are going into vertical structures to scale, X-ray is needed to detect defects deeper in the 3D chips, said Byron Gill, managing partner at Indus. Rigaku might be one of the few companies that "has the key to unlocking scale for the semiconductor industry in the middle of a super cycle", he added, forecasting a 100% rise in its valuation by 2029. REFORM THEME DOMINATES The corporate reform theme still has a long way to run, market participants said. "Japan changes slowly, but once the change starts, it does not reverse," said Naohide Une, partner and CEO at Investment Lab, a former senior managing director at Japan Post Bank. He picked Japanese chemical company Ube Corporation (4208.T) for its corporate reform efforts. In a separate Q&A session, Seth Fischer, founder of activist Oasis Management, said his fund may substantially increase its stake in Japanese electric motor maker Nidec (6594.T) . AI AS A BACK-OFFICE TAILWIND AI was another key investment theme. Investment firms Ruane Cunniff and Japan Catalyst picked software companies Money Forward (3994.T) and OBIC Business Consultants (4733.T) , respectively. They argued that back-office software operators are AI winners rather than losers, as clients require accuracy. And these businesses are helping Japan overcome labor tightness, they said.

item.title: Dólar se encamina a caída semanal por menor expectativa de alza de tasas de la Fed
item.description: El dólar bajaba el viernes, en camino a su primera caída semanal en más de un mes frente al euro y al yen, en medio de menores expectativas de un alza de tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal y preocupaciones por una ola de ventas en las bolsas impulsada por la inteligencia artificial.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Rebaudo, Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: El dólar bajaba el viernes, en camino a su primera caída semanal en más de un mes frente al euro y al yen, en medio de menores expectativas de un alza de tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal y preocupaciones por una ola de ventas en las bolsas impulsada por la inteligencia artificial. * Los mercados se vieron sacudidos esta semana por datos de precios al consumo y a la producción más altos de lo esperado. * No obstante, las autoridades de la Fed aseguraron que no hay urgencia por endurecer la política monetaria, contribuyendo a estabilizar el rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro y minando el apoyo al dólar. * Las acciones del sector de la IA cayeron esta semana y la tensión se extendió a sectores del mercado crediticio, ya que los inversores a lo largo de toda la cadena de suministro temen ahora que los operadores de centros de datos no logren ser rentables a tiempo para pagar sus deudas. * "Desde mediados de junio, con un Comité Federal de Mercado Abierto de tono agresivo, las tasas han estado impulsando el dólar, y ahora parece que la preocupación sobre la sostenibilidad de la IA están contrarrestando ese efecto", dijo Marc Chandler, de Bannockburn Capital Markets. * El índice dólar , que compara al billete verde con una cesta de seis destacadas divisas, caía un 0,42% a 101,61 unidades, en camino a un descenso semanal del 0,6%. * La libra esterlina ganaba un 0,6%, a 1,3353 dólares, con un alza acumulada del 0,92% en la semana, mientras que el dólar restaba un 0,48% ante el franco suizo, al 0,8228%, lo que supone un declive semanal del 0,92%. * El euro subía un 0,33%, a 1,1255 dólares, tras mejorar un 0,56% el jueves, su mayor avance diario en dos meses y en camino a un alza semanal del 0,48%. Frente al yen, el dólar cedía un 0,12%, a 157,79 unidades, cerca de poner fin a cuatro semanas seguidas a la baja.

item.title: 欧州、債務持続性へ成長加速と赤字削減を＝ＩＭＦ
item.description:
Jan Strupczewski
［バンコク １６日 ロイター］ - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１６日、欧州各国が公的債...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州、債務持続性へ成長加速と赤字削減を＝ＩＭＦ 10/16 20:59 配信

国際通貨基金（IMF）のロゴ、ワシントンの本部で2024年撮影 REUTERS/Benoit Tessier/File Photo

Jan Strupczewski

［バンコク　１６日　ロイター］ - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１６日、欧州各国が公的債務を持続可能な水準に維持するには成長を加速させるか、借り入れを減らす必要があるとし、「何もしないという選択肢はない」と警告した。

ＩＭＦは１３日、ユーロ圏の経済成長率について、４月時点と同じく２０２６年が１．１％、２７年は１．２％と予想した。インフレ率は、２６年が３．１％、２７年が２．８％、２８年が２．２％になると予測した。

ＩＭＦは「債務の持続可能性を保つには、欧州諸国の約４分の３で、成長を高めて歳出圧力を緩和する構造改革と、中期的に国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比で平均約３．５％に相当する財政赤字削減策を組み合わせる必要がある」と指摘した。

欧州連合（ＥＵ）全加盟国が欧州委員会と合意しなければならない「中期財政・構造計画」で予定されている財政再建規模はＧＤＰ比で平均約２％にとどまり、一部の国で必要とされる水準を下回っているという。

「スタッフの基本予測は、大半の国で財政再建が計画を下回ることを示しており、想定されている再建規模でさえ達成が困難となる恐れがある」と指摘。

「欧州諸国の約４分の１は、公的債務を持続可能にするためにＧＤＰ比で５％超の財政再建が必要となる。これは過去に実行可能と証明された水準を上回っており、政府活動の範囲を見直し、不足分を補うために民間部門の役割を拡大する以外に選択肢はない」と分析した。

欧州委が５月に発表した予測によると、ＥＵ全体の債務の対ＧＤＰ比率は、２５年末時点の８２．８％から２６年に８４．２％、２７年末までには８５．３％へ上昇する見通し。ユーロ圏の比率も２５年の８８．７％から２６年に９０．２％に上昇し、２７年には９１．２％に達すると予測されている。

ＩＭＦ欧州局長のマテウシュ・シュチュレク氏はロイターに対し、「高齢化、国防費増額、エネルギー移行など、欧州の大半の国が直面している長期的な歳出課題を勘案すると、政策変更がなければ欧州の平均的な経済において公的債務は大幅に増加し、現在の水準の最大２倍に達する可能性がある」と述べ、中欧の高成長国の一部では、この債務拡大のペースがさらに速くなる可能性があるとした。

「持続可能性の定義が（債務の）増大を止めて安定化させられるかどうかであるなら、財政面での対応と再建が不可欠だ」とし、「より早く動く方が常に対処費用は少なくて済む。着手が遅れるほど調整は難しくなる」と語った。

ＩＭＦは欧州の成長加速に向けた最大の障害は低水準の生産性だと指摘し、各国政府に対してＥＵ域内市場の障壁を取り除き、技術革新（イノベーション）や事業拡大への投資を行うよう求めた。

「一定の改革に向けた取り組みが進められているものの、未完成のＥＵ単一市場と各国の障壁が、企業の事業調整や規模拡大、より大きな市場へのアクセスを困難にしている」とした。

また、化石燃料から再生可能エネルギーへの移行を継続し、重要鉱物を含む世界的なサプライチェーン（供給網）の多様化を進めるよう呼びかけた。これらは全てＥＵが既に取り組んでいる政策方針となる。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：年初来安値で確認する円の「現在地」、円安は欧州通貨高の裏返し＝唐鎌大輔氏 コラム：短距離フライト削減でＣＯ2対策なるか、的外れの欧州 焦点：コーヒー企業「アフリカ離れ」も、ＥＵが森林破壊防止法 アングル：欧州熱波、マクロ経済面からの市場注目ポイント コラム：米だけ「異世界」のＩＭＦ会合　イラン戦争無視で政権の苦境露呈 最終更新: 10/16(金) 20:59 ロイター

item.title: Shell agrees proposed sale of French fuel stations to DCC Energy, source says
item.description: Shell has agreed a deal with Dublin-based DCC Energy for the proposed sale of its network of fuel retail stations and related transport-fuels services in France, according to a person familiar with the matter and documents seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Kelly, Dimitri Rhodes
item.content:encoded: Shell (SHEL.L) has agreed a deal with Dublin-based DCC Energy for the proposed sale of its network of fuel retail stations and related transport-fuels services in France, according to a person familiar with the matter and documents seen by Reuters. The agreement comes as Shell aims to focus its fuel retail and charging operations on key markets where it generates the majority of its cash flow, including the US, Canada and the United Kingdom. The parties have yet to finalise the deal, although completion is expected in the second quarter of 2027, subject to consultation with employee representatives, the document showed. The transaction would include around 70 sites, eight LNG installations and the transfer of 35 employees, the document showed. "Shell is considering a sale of its retail forecourts business in France," Shell told Reuters, adding that it would not comment further at this stage. DCC Energy declined to comment. DCC Energy, a sales and distribution company in Europe and the US, serves millions of customers across the industrial and public sectors and delivers off-grid energy solutions, led by liquid gas, the company's website said. It also operates service stations and fleet services. DCC Energy would operate the stations under a long-term Shell brand licence, the document showed. However, Shell's core fuel supply operations are excluded, meaning the buyer would source its fuel independently. The monetary value of the deal could not immediately be determined. Shell's marketing unit, which includes its fuel and charging retail stations, reported $1.3 billion in adjusted earnings in the second quarter this year, compared with $1.2 billion during the same time last year.

item.title: 仏借り入れコスト上昇、長期化なら財政健全化圧力高まる＝ＩＭＦ
item.description:
Jan Strupczewski
[バンコク １６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のシュチュレク欧州局長はフ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
仏借り入れコスト上昇、長期化なら財政健全化圧力高まる＝ＩＭＦ 10/16 20:55 配信

シュチュレクＩＭＦ欧州局長、１４日撮影 REUTERS/Patipat Janthong

Jan Strupczewski

[バンコク １６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のシュチュレク欧州局長はフランスの借り入れコストが上がっていることについて、短期的には対処できるとの見方を示した。ただ上昇が続けば２０２７年予算だけでなく、信頼性のある中期的な財政健全化計画の策定を求める圧力が強まると指摘した。

シュチュレク氏はバンコクで開かれているＩＭＦ年次総会の合間にロイターの取材に応じた。現時点では仏国債市場はまだ秩序立った動きを保っているとの認識を示した。

「（市場には）流動性があり、（国債の）償還期間もかなり長く、投資家層も多様だ。銀行の流動性が高いことも支えになっている。このため短期的な債務リスクには十分対応できる」と語った。

一方、「利回りの高止まりが長引けば、財政とコスト抑制への圧力が強まる。財政の不均衡是正が急務であることを改めて認識させる。まずは２７年予算から着手すべきで、欧州連合（ＥＵ）の財政ルールに沿って遅滞なく承認される必要がある」と述べた。

フランスは２６年の財政赤字を国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比５．４％と見込む。２７年は５．０％への引き下げを目標としている。ＥＵの法令を順守するには、２９年までに赤字をＧＤＰ比３％未満に抑える必要がある。

シュチュレク氏は「それは確かに必要だ。市場の動きは、われわれにもフランスの政策当局者にも、その必要性を改めて認識させている」とし「市場のシグナルには政策を変える力がある。過去に何度も見てきた。ある意味では、債券市場から現実を突き付けられることで、財政調整のあり方が変わり、調整が加速する可能性がある」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：米国債の「ベーシス取引」、軟着陸は可能か コラム：米財務省の借入拡大、債務問題の大きさに比べれば単なるノイズ 焦点：仏、財政赤字巡り政局緊迫　大統領選控え市場の不安と格下げ警戒 コラム：米だけ「異世界」のＩＭＦ会合　イラン戦争無視で政権の苦境露呈 最終更新: 10/16(金) 20:55 ロイター

item.title: Oro anota caída semanal mientras los operadores analizan las señales de la Fed
item.description: Los precios del oro se mantuvieron prácticamente estables el viernes pero anotaron una caída semanal mientras los operadores sopesaban la posibilidad de nuevas alzas de tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal este año tras una serie de datos de inflación en Estados Unidos más altos de lo esperado.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Sinha
item.content:encoded: Los precios del oro se mantuvieron prácticamente estables el viernes pero anotaron una caída semanal mientras los operadores sopesaban la posibilidad de nuevas alzas de tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal este año tras una serie de datos de inflación en Estados Unidos más altos de lo esperado. El oro al contado subió un 0,1% a 4.175,66 dólares por onza a las 1543 GMT, pero acumuló un descenso del 0,4% en la semana. Los futuros del oro estadounidense con entrega en diciembre subieron un 0,6% hasta los 4.196,40 dólares por onza. "Nos encontramos en un rango muy estrecho y nos inclinamos hacia el límite inferior de soporte, debido principalmente a que sigue habiendo mucha incertidumbre sobre lo que hará la Fed", afirmó Bart Melek, director global de estrategia de materias primas de TD Securities. El presidente de la Reserva Federal, Kevin Warsh, se mostró optimista sobre la solidez de la economía estadounidense, pero no dio pistas sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés del banco central. Los datos publicados el jueves revelaron que los precios al productor de Estados Unidos registraron el mes pasado su mayor subida en cuatro años y medio. Estos datos se sumaron al informe sobre los precios al consumo del miércoles, que mostraba una aceleración de los precios en septiembre. El presidente de la Fed de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, calificó los datos de "desalentadores", mientras que la presidenta de la Fed de Cleveland, Beth Hammack, señaló que la Fed podría verse obligada a subir las tasas de interés de forma más agresiva si se produjera un deterioro notable de las expectativas de inflación del público. Los operadores esperan en su mayoría que el banco central estadounidense mantenga las tasas estables este mes, al tiempo que descuentan una probabilidad del 90% de que se produzca una subida de tasas en diciembre, según la herramienta FedWatch. Aunque el oro suele considerarse una cobertura contra la inflación, el aumento de las tasas de interés tiende a reducir el atractivo de este metal que no genera rendimiento. "Durante lo que queda de año, es probable que los precios del oro bajen ligeramente, a medida que la Fed siga subiendo las tasas y los temores en torno al fin del auge de la IA resulten ser temporales", afirmó Hamad Hussain, economista especializado en clima y materias primas de Capital Economics. Entre otros metales, la plata al contado se mantuvo estable en 57,43 dólares por onza, el platino subió un 0,6% a 1.636 dólares y el paladio bajó un 0,2% a 1.124,25 dólares. Los tres metales anotaron pérdidas semanales.

Strategy faces MSCI ouster under new rules, billions in passive holdings at risk

FILE PHOTO: Michael Saylor, Chairman of the Board of Directors and Chief Executive Office of MicroStrategy Inc, speaks during the Bitcoin Conference 2023, in Miami Beach, Florida, U.S., May 19, 2023. REUTERS/Marco Bello/File Photo

FAST

Oct 16 : Michael Saylor's Strategy faces potential removal from MSCI's global equity indexes under new rules adopted on Thursday, threatening billions of dollars in passive investment in the bitcoin buyer. Shares of Strategy, the world's biggest corporate bitcoin holder and a constituent of the MSCI USA and MSCI World indexes, fell 4.2 per cent on Friday. MSCI said on Thursday non-operating companies will be ineligible for its Global Investable Market Indexes from the close of November 30, as part of its November index review. It will publish the final list of affected companies on November 11. The decision follows a review MSCI began a year ago, when it proposed excluding digital asset treasury companies on the grounds that they resemble investment funds, which are already barred from its indexes. MSCI deferred that plan in January and opened a broader review on all non-operating companies.

MSCI defines non-operating companies as investment funds and business development companies, and other companies whose finances make them look like one. Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet are on MSCI's list of potential deletions. SharpLink and several other crypto treasury companies are on a watchlist for possible removal. The changes are aimed at expanding MSCI’s exclusions for passive investment vehicles, with companies required to meet financial tests on their operating assets to remain eligible. Index inclusion matters to companies such as Strategy because passive funds and other investors tracking benchmarks are required to hold their shares. Strategy did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The company warned last year that an exclusion would result in $2.8 billion of its stock being liquidated and would "chill" the industry. Strategy, which pioneered the model of raising money through stock and debt sales to buy bitcoin, had a market value of about $64.3 billion on Friday. Its shares were down 4.8 per cent in 2026.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Swiss journalist risks court sentence for exposing top banker
item.description: Zurich prosecutors this week charged Swiss journalist Lukas Haessig with violating banking secrecy over reporting that set off a high-profile corporate criminal trial of the former boss of Raiffeisen Bank Switzerland, Haessig said on his financial blog Inside Paradeplatz.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Zurich prosecutors this week charged Swiss journalist Lukas Haessig with violating banking secrecy over reporting that set off a high-profile corporate criminal trial of the former boss of Raiffeisen Bank Switzerland, Haessig said on his financial blog Inside Paradeplatz. Zurich-based Inside Paradeplatz published a series of articles in 2016 about Pierin Vincenz, former CEO of Raiffeisen Bank Switzerland, and his business partner Beat Stocker, who were found guilty of fraud in April 2022 That verdict [USN:L8N4422LC TEXT:"is currently under review"] by a higher court expected to rule in January 2027 Police in June 2025 searched the blog's Zurich office and home of its founder, seizing evidence linked to suspected violation of Swiss banking law Prosecutors had dropped the case in December 2025, but Zurich's High Court in April said a court must decide how the banking secrecy provision should be interpreted after a complaint by Stocker Article 47 of the Swiss Banking Act criminalises disclosure of confidential information leaked by bank insiders, with penalties of up to three years in prison or a fine Press freedom group Reporters Without Borders Switzerland called the charges troubling and said Article 47 of the Swiss banking act must not be used to prosecute journalists Inside Paradeplatz's reporting was clearly in the public interest, Reporters Without Borders said, adding the banking secrecy law had a chilling effect and pointing to "legal shortcomings" in Switzerland on press freedom Prosecutors said the presumption of innocence applies to Haessig. No court date has yet been set

item.title: トヨタ、30年までに全車種をＳＤＶに 年1000万台の新車に独自ソフト搭載
item.description: [東京 １６日 ロイター] - トヨタ自動車は、２０３０年までに世界で販売する全５０車種を「ソフトウエア定義車両（Ｓ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
トヨタ、30年までに全車種をＳＤＶに　年1000万台の新車に独自ソフト搭載 10/16 20:20 配信

トヨタ自動車の「ＲＡＶ４」。２０２５年５月、東京で撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Manami Yamada）

[東京 １６日 ロイター] - トヨタ自動車は、２０３０年までに世界で販売する全５０車種を「ソフトウエア定義車両（ＳＤＶ）」にする。独自のソフトウェアプラットフォーム（基盤）「Ａｒｅｎｅ（アリーン）」を新車に順次搭載する。ＳＤＶで先行する中国や米国の電気自動車（ＥＶ）メーカーを追撃し、年間１０００万台規模の新車販売に加え、売った後もソフトの更新などを通じて課金するビジネスモデルを強化する。

同社広報によると、中嶋裕樹副社長が先週、アリーンの導入計画をベルギーのブリュッセルで投資家に説明。３５年にはトヨタ車以外にも展開し、提携先など他社の車両にアリーンを供給する考えも明らかにしたという。

トヨタは２５年に発売したスポーツ多目的車（ＳＵＶ）「ＲＡＶ４」で初めてアリーンを導入し、今後販売する新車に順次展開する方針を示唆していた。

ＳＤＶは、スマートフォンのように購入後も無線通信を通じてソフトを更新し、先進運転支援技術やエンタテイメントなど車の性能や機能を向上させる車で、米テスラや中国勢が先行している。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：サウジを揺さぶるフーシ派、攻撃力向上の背景は アングル：米国の「軽油ショック」、消費者の身の回りで着実に進行 コラム：トヨタ自動車、ＨＶ技術活用で再び成長軌道へ 焦点：トヨタの中国合弁2社に再編機運、市場縮小と競争激化で転換点 焦点：トヨタ社長、3年でなぜ交代　インフレが変えた時代の潮流 最終更新: 10/16(金) 20:20 ロイター

item.title: UK's FTSE 100 logs strongest week in six months on defensive-sector rally
item.description: Britain's blue-chip stocks had their best week in six months, as investors flocking to defensive sectors offset a rout in AI-linked stocks, while finance minister John Healey's reassurances on fiscal discipline also helped risk appetite.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's blue-chip stocks had their best week in six months, as investors flocking to defensive sectors offset a rout in AI-linked stocks, while finance minister John Healey's reassurances on fiscal discipline also helped risk appetite. The export-heavy FTSE 100 (.FTSE) closed 0.38% higher at 10,881.90 points, logging a weekly gain of 3.1%, the biggest since early April, while the midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) gained 0.45%. UK's large-cap ETFs attracted $3.38 billion in estimated net inflows year to date, already the biggest annual total since 2020, data from Morningstar showed "Flows into passive funds typically follow performance, but they also reflect investors looking to diversify away from US mega-cap technology and broaden their equity exposure," said Michael Born, an analyst at Morningstar Consumer staples supported gains. Cigarette maker British American Tobacco (BATS.L) rose 2.1%, while Johnnie Walker owner Diageo (DGE.L) gained 1.9% The beverages (.FTNMX451010) and medical equipment and services (.FTNMX201020) sectors advanced 7.8% and 6.9%, respectively, in the week Homebuilders (.FTNMX402020) jumped over 6% in the week after Healey [USN:S8N4040BJ TEXT:"reaffirmed"] his commitment to fiscal discipline on Thursday Banks (.FTNMX301010) were muted on Friday, recovering from early losses triggered by a [USN:SPN46001Q TEXT:"report"] that Healey was likely to tax the lenders in the budget Bank of England [USN:L1N46202H TEXT:"Governor Andrew Bailey"] said signs of second-round inflation were limited ahead of next week's inflation data Traders are pricing in four BoE rate hikes over the next 12 months, according to LSEG data Defence stocks (.FTNMX502010) extended a strong run on the day: BAE Systems (BAES.L) and Babcock International (BAB.L) rose 2.6% and 3.6%, respectively THG (THG.L) had its best week in six months, surging 30% after the e-commerce firm raised its annual adjusted core profit forecast on Thursday

item.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq set for steep weekly losses as AI jitters rattle investors
item.description: The benchmark S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set to end the week in the red, with technology stocks coming under more pressure on Friday over cracks in the AI trade and adding to losses.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Purvi Agarwal
item.content:encoded: The benchmark S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set to end the week in the red, with technology stocks coming under more pressure on Friday over cracks in the AI trade and adding to losses. The S&P 500 information technology index (.SPLRCT) fell 1.5% and was the biggest drag. [USN:L6N4620IB TEXT:"Nvidia-backed"] CoreWeave (CRWV.O) slid 10.3% on lingering debt concerns. The data centre operator's bonds sold off sharply this week, pushing yields to above 15%. Semiconductors bore the brunt of the selloff, with the broader chips index (.SOX) dropping 1.8% — set for its steepest eight-session percentage decline since the "Liberation Day" selloff in April 2025. Most megacap stocks tumbled and brought the Nasdaq close to a one-month low. Meta (META.O) slipped 2.3% and Microsoft (MSFT.O) lost 1.8%. AI stocks have cratered this week over concerns that data centre operators might not turn profitable in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise. Worries over rising competition from China also dented sentiment. "When investors start worrying that AI names are overvalued, they gravitate toward lower-multiple stocks with stable cash flows," said Dennis Dick, founder and market structure analyst at Triple D Trading. Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors [USN:L6N4611DN TEXT:"are weighing a lower valuation"] for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. At 12:19 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 14.74 points, or 0.03%, to 52,162.95, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 43.53 points, or 0.56%, to 7,700.38 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) lost 348.31 points, or 1.30%, to 26,364.72. Most other S&P 500 sectors rose. The energy index (.SPNY) was the biggest percentage gainer, up 1.5%, while the financials index (.SPSY) rose 1%. Gains in Goldman Sachs (GS.N) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) lifted the Dow to its highest level in over a month. The index is set for a weekly advance, with investors rushing to defensive sectors such as healthcare and consumer staples. "What we're seeing now is money rotating out of a very crowded AI trade and into value names," Dick added. The S&P 500 was set for its steepest weekly loss since early June, faced with an AI-led rout, mixed bank earnings and inflation data. The Nasdaq eyed its sharpest weekly fall since June 22. Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week have confirmed that price pressures are extending beyond energy products. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh also said a spending surge was boosting inflation, but added that the US [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"economy"] remained resilient and benefited from the AI-driven investment boom. Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays [USN:FWN4622T4 TEXT:"now expects"] 25 basis point hikes each in December and January. Meanwhile, Tesla (TSLA.O) failed to hold on to gains from before the bell — as much as 3% — after unveiling a [USN:L1N46200L TEXT:"redesigned Roadster"], powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX. Netflix (NFLX.O) [USN:L4N46128P TEXT:"appointed"] former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares were down 2.6%. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.04-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.94-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted 17 new 52-week highs and no new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 46 new highs and 200 new lows.

item.title: France, Germany strike deal on car emissions and UK special status
item.description: France and Germany struck a deal on Friday to soften proposed EU car emissions rules and open the door for Britain to be treated as a trusted partner under the bloc's Made in EU rules.
item.dc:creator: Philip Blenkinsop
item.content:encoded: France and Germany struck a deal on Friday to soften proposed EU car emissions rules and open the door for Britain to be treated as a trusted partner under the bloc's [USN:L6N45E0Q1 TEXT:""Made in EU" rules"]. The European Commission [USN:L6N3XM0EA TEXT:"proposed last year"] that automakers cut CO2 emissions by 90% from 2021 levels in 2035, with the remaining 10% offset through measures such as the use of low-carbon steel and alternative fuels. Under the Franco-German plan, the 2035 target would be set at 90%, but without the need for additional compensatory measures. The approach is broadly in line with the wishes of German automakers. European automotive stocks gained after the deal was announced, lifting the STOXX 600 Automobile and Parts Index (.SXAP) nearly 2%. The joint plan also addresses an EU proposal introducing local-content and low-carbon requirements for products bought through public procurement, public auctions or subsidy schemes. France has pushed for these products to be limited to those manufactured in the European Union. Other EU members, including Germany, argue that countries closely linked to EU automotive supply chains and free-trade-agreement partners should also be included. The Franco-German plan says that for the automotive sector, "Made in EU" should cover the EU's 27 countries and other European partners that were part of the EU internal market on January 1, 2020. That would include Britain, which left the EU single market at the end of 2020. Volkswagen , Europe's largest automaker, said the compromise would help the industry contribute "to climate protection without jeopardizing its competitiveness." The German company said the "Made in EU" proposals "provide a clear incentive for production and investment in Europe". An official at British Prime Minister Andy Burnham's Downing Street office said inclusion in the "Made in EU" scheme would boost Britain's automotive sector. However, he said the Franco-German proposal requires wider European backing and that details had yet to be seen. The Franco-German plan also says that inclusion should be subject to an agreement on full reciprocity, along with "dynamic alignment with EU conditions for investment from third countries and with EU trade protection measures". That could mean Britain adopting measures the EU has taken to [USN:L6N45V0LF TEXT:"restrict imports"] of Chinese-built hybrid and battery-electric vehicles. Speaking to reporters in London, Renault (RENA.PA) CEO Francois Provost said "obviously, the UK should be part of" the "Made in the EU" scheme as it is part of Europe's automotive "ecosystem." But he said Britain should in turn ditch its [USN:L8N446056 TEXT:"EV sales mandate"] and adopt the same rules as the EU. "The two automotive industrial policies should be consistent," Provost said. A GOOD DAY FOR JOBS OR A 'HISTORIC MISTAKE'? The Franco-German paper also proposed compliance periods spanning multiple years for CO2 emission targets, no revision before 2030 of the utility factor for hybrid vehicles, which measures the share of driving done electrically, and recognition of cars powered by renewable and low-carbon fuels as zero-emission vehicles. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the deal "a good day for motorists and for jobs in Germany, France and Europe", adding that Italy largely agreed with the proposals. The deal will not please all automakers. Toyota's (7203.T) European division, which sells cars in Europe from plants in the EU, Britain, Turkey and Japan, said on Thursday that including partners such as Britain, Canada, Japan, South Korea and Turkey would give the EU the scale needed to compete with China. [USN:L1N45Z0LF TEXT:"Turkey's trade minister"] said this week on a trip to Brussels that trusted partners like Turkey should not be excluded. Green and environmental groups criticised the emissions proposals. German Greens lawmaker Swantje Michaelsen said Germany's government was holding back the industry as high fuel prices accelerate EV demand. Anna Krajinska of transport and environment campaign group T&E called the deal a "historic mistake" that would reduce the incentive for automakers to invest in EVs. "German and French political leaders claim they are acting to save jobs, but this may well be the deal that buries Europe’s auto industry," she said. France and Germany must convince other EU members and the European Parliament for their plans to enter into force. They are unlikely to reach a final common text before early next year, after an EU-UK summit planned for November 20.

item.title: El cobre impulsa al alza el complejo metalero antes de la LME Week
item.description: Los precios del cobre impulsaron al alza a otros metales básicos el viernes, gracias al apoyo que supuso la debilidad del dólar, mientras que los mercados bursátiles se estabilizaban tras la fuerte caída del jueves en los valores tecnológicos, mejorando el apetito por el riesgo por los metales dependientes del crecimiento.
item.dc:creator: Polina Devitt
item.content:encoded: Los precios del cobre impulsaron al alza a otros metales básicos el viernes, gracias al apoyo que supuso la debilidad del dólar, mientras que los mercados bursátiles se estabilizaban tras la fuerte caída del jueves en los valores tecnológicos, mejorando el apetito por el riesgo por los metales dependientes del crecimiento. * A las 1600 GMT, el contrato de referencia del cobre a tres meses en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres (LME) ganó un 0,3%, a 14.384 dólares por tonelada, recuperándose del mínimo de casi dos semanas de 14.256 dólares alcanzado el jueves. * La reunión anual LME Week, que se celebrará la próxima semana en Londres y a la que acuden consumidores, productores, operadores y corredores del sector de los metales, coincide con el tercer miércoles del mes, fecha en la que vencen los contratos mensuales de la LME. * El cobre y el zinc, junto con el aluminio y el estaño, se encaminan hacia la próxima semana en situación de "backwardation", con los contratos al contado cotizando con una prima respecto a los contratos a tres meses, una estructura que apunta a cierta escasez en la oferta a corto plazo. * "La verdadera escasez de cobre refinado este año se ha debido a que el metal refinado ha seguido inundando el mercado estadounidense ante la perspectiva de los aranceles previstos para enero del año que viene", afirmó Ian Roper, investigador de metales de la correduría Marex, en una presentación. * Sin embargo, Roper prevé que el cobre se vea sometido a presión de cara a fines de año, ya que a principios de diciembre comienza a cerrarse el plazo para que los envíos pasen la aduana estadounidense antes de que termine el año, lo que liberará parte del metal para los mercados fuera de Estados Unidos. * El cobre acumula un alza del 16% en lo que va de año, tras tocar un máximo histórico de 14.875 dólares hace cinco semanas. * Entre otros metales básicos de la LME, el aluminio subió un 0,5%, a 3.001 dólares por tonelada; el zinc ganó un 0,7%, a 3.690,5 dólares; el níquel avanzó un 0,7%, a 15.325 dólares; el plomo mejoró un 0,4%, a 1.887 dólares; y el estaño sumó un 0,3%, a 50.240 dólares.

(Corrects headline and first paragraph to say Waymo is owned by Alphabet, not Google) Oct 16 : Alphabet's Waymo said on Friday it plans to bring its autonomous ride-hailing service to Toronto in 2028, marking the self-driving company's first planned deployment in Canada and its latest move to expand beyond the US. Here are some details: • Waymo, which operates commercial robotaxi services in several US cities, said it would partner with Element Fleet Management for fleet operations in Toronto as it expands to markets including London and Tokyo • The company said it will begin groundwork in Canada's largest city, including mapping and engagement with local authorities, as it prepares for a future deployment of the Waymo Driver. • Waymo also plans to create hundreds of jobs over time in fleet maintenance, validation driving, customer service and other operations functions

AMSTERDAM, Oct 16 : Shares in computer chip packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) fell 3 per cent on Friday after influential semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis reported that one of the company's main growth products will face competition from bigger rival ASML. The SemiAnalysis report analysed 27 patent filings by ASML, which it said indicated ASML was developing a hybrid bonding product. Besi is a fraction of the size of ASML, the biggest maker of equipment used to make semiconductors, but Besi is a leader in hybrid bonding, an advanced packaging technology being used to create a new generation of more powerful three-dimensional chips.   ASML has not confirmed it is developing such a tool. Besi did not respond to requests for comment.

Besi shares were down 3 per cent at €158.50, while ASML was up 1.1 per cent at €1,480 in midday Amsterdam trading. A spokesperson for ASML declined to comment on the SemiAnalysis report but pointed to the company's launch of its first advanced packaging tool last year. "We continue to look at which directions the 3D integration industry will evolve ... and where ASML's expertise can be of additional value," the company said in a statement at that time. In March, Reuters reported that ASML was planning additional packaging tools, citing Chief Technical Officer Marco Pieters in an interview. "The semiconductor market has already signalled that packaging is one of those next frontiers where performance gains can be unlocked, and ASML seems to be building next-gen tools headed in the same direction," said Nick Rossolillo, co-founder of Chip Stock Investor. "We see the new batch of packaging tools, beyond an EUV pipeline, as critical to pulling off the growth needed to justify (ASML's) elevated valuation."

item.title: イスラエル人入植者、ヨルダン川西岸でオリーブ収穫中の村人襲撃
item.description:
Pesha Magid
[アブファラ（ヨルダン川西岸） １６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Pesha Magid

[アブファラ（ヨルダン川西岸） １６日 ロイター] - 覆面をしたイスラエル人入植者数十人が１６日、パレスチナ自治区ヨルダン川西岸の村でオリーブを収穫していた村人を組織的に襲撃し、木を焼いたり、石を投げたりした。記者を含む少なくとも２人が負傷した。

現場を目撃したロイター記者によると、オリーブの実を摘むためにアブファラの村人が畑に集まっていたところ、入植者約８０人が畑を見下ろす丘から下りてきた。一部は投石器を使い、村人たちに向けて石を放ったという。

襲撃のさなか、イスラエル軍のジープ少なくとも２台が土ぼこりを上げながら現場一帯を走行した。軍の到着後も襲撃は続き、イスラエル兵はジープを避けて逃げたパレスチナ人に向けて催涙ガスを発射した。

現場では実弾の発砲音が聞こえた。ロイターの写真記者は武装した入植者少なくとも１人が銃を撃つのを目撃した。

イスラエル軍はコメント要請に応じていない。

パレスチナの医療関係者によると、２人が負傷し、ラマラ周辺の病院に搬送された。うち１人は米紙ワシントン・ポストの写真記者だった。

アブファラでの襲撃に先立ち、１６日朝にはトゥルムスアヤ村周辺でも同様の襲撃があった。入植者らはオリーブを収穫していた農家の集団を襲い、車３台に火を付けた。

イスラエルの入植活動を監視する人権団体「イェシュ・ディン」によると、占領下のヨルダン川西岸では、イスラエル人入植者によるパレスチナ人への暴力が急増している。オリーブ収穫が始まった頃にあたる９月２７日以降、少なくとも１７０件の襲撃が起きた。

ネタニヤフ首相は暴力を批判しているが、取り締まりに向けた措置はほとんど講じていない。

item.title: ペトロチャイナ、取引部門の26年利益が過去最高に 中東情勢の影響回避
item.description:
Chen Aizhu
[シンガポール １６日 ロイター] - 中国石油天然気（ペトロチャイナ）で、原油などの取引を手...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ペトロチャイナ、取引部門の26年利益が過去最高に　中東情勢の影響回避 10/16 19:33 配信

ペトロチャイナのロゴ、メディア向け視察ツアーで6月撮影 REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov

Chen Aizhu

[シンガポール １６日 ロイター] - 中国石油天然気（ペトロチャイナ）で、原油などの取引を手掛けるトレーディング部門の２０２６年の利益が過去最高を更新する見通しであることが、複数の関係者の話で分かった。イラン紛争によって中東産原油の売買形態が一変し、需給が逼迫する中、中国国外の製油所の利幅が大幅に拡大している。

アジア最大の石油・天然ガス生産会社で中国第２位の石油精製会社であるペトロチャイナは、大規模な生産・供給ポートフォリオと広範な精製・小売りネットワークを生かして利益を上げ、戦争に伴う供給混乱の影響を回避できている。

事情に詳しい関係者２人によると、ペトロチャイナのトレーディング部門、中国石油国際事業（ＰＣＩ）の２６年粗利益は２００億元（３０億ドル）を超え過去最高になる見込み。

同部門の幹部によると、通常、ＰＣＩ部門利益の半分以上を稼ぎ出す原油部門の利益が１０月初旬までに、２５年通年の２倍以上に達したほか、石油製品部門や天然ガス部門も好調に推移している。

同社は決算でトレーディング部門利益の内訳を開示していない。８月に発表した上半期グループ純利益は約１４６億５０００万ドルだった。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：サウジを揺さぶるフーシ派、攻撃力向上の背景は アングル：米国の「軽油ショック」、消費者の身の回りで着実に進行 アングル：ＡＩ株売りに勢い、資金調達に懸念　クライマックスには距離 アングル：ＥＵの自動車現地調達ルール案、中国勢は先回りで足場固め アングル：金価格、米国債利回り上昇でも4000ドル台維持　中銀の準備資産分散が下支え 最終更新: 10/16(金) 19:33 ロイター

item.title: Trudy forecast to near Mexico's Pacific coast as major hurricane through the weekend
item.description: Hurricane Trudy rapidly intensified on Friday, carrying maximum winds near 120 mph (195 kph), and is expected to approach Mexico's Pacific coast as a major storm during the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Aida Pelaez-fernandez
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Trudy rapidly intensified on Friday, carrying maximum winds near 120 mph (195 kph), and is expected to approach Mexico's Pacific coast as a major storm during the weekend. Additional strengthening is still forecast before Trudy nears the coast of Jalisco and Colima states late on Saturday as a life-threatening major hurricane, Mexican authorities and the US-based National Hurricane Center warned. It is not expected to make landfall but will remain very close to the coast, about 60 to 65 km away, and any change in its path closer to shore will increase the severity of its impact, the head of Mexico's weather agency Fabian Vazquez said at a press conference. "Everyone in this region needs to be very careful and stay alert over the weekend," he added. Mexico's civil protection agency asked residents to start preparations for the storm's arrival by securing doors and windows, and removing objects that could be thrown around by the strong winds. "Trudy has the potential to even reach Category 4 or 5 intensity," said Alex DaSilva, a hurricane meteorologist at private forecaster AccuWeather. Located about 235 miles (380 km) southwest of resort city Acapulco, the storm is expected to produce up to 15 inches (38 cm) of rain in the states of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco, increasing the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, according to the NHC. HARD-HIT PACIFIC COAST The hurricane will strike Mexico's Pacific coast, a region that has already been battered in recent weeks by storms that left several dead and caused severe flooding. "The most critical conditions will start on Saturday, with very severe winds and waves along the coast, in an area that has already been affected for several weeks," Vazquez said. Tropical Storm Simon continues to weaken farther northwest offshore, after [USN:L1N45Y0H6 TEXT:"dropping heavy rain"] along the coast earlier as a hurricane. Last week, tropical storm Rachel hit the Baja California peninsula damaging 1,500 homes, according to Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum.

item.title: Barril sube más de 3% para registrar alza semanal, mercado atento a suministro O.Medio
item.description: Los precios del petróleo subieron más de un 3% para registrar un avance semanal, debido a la continua incertidumbre sobre el suministro en Oriente Medio, mientras los inversionistas seguían evaluando la cantidad de gasóleo que Rusia podría suministrar a los mercados mundiales.
item.dc:creator: Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: Los precios del petróleo subieron más de un 3% para registrar un avance semanal, debido a la continua incertidumbre sobre el suministro en Oriente Medio, mientras los inversionistas seguían evaluando la cantidad de gasóleo que Rusia podría suministrar a los mercados mundiales. * Los futuros del crudo Brent se disparaban 3 dólares a un máximo de sesión de 109,58 dólares el barril a las 1650 GMT, mientras que los futuros del crudo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) de Estados Unidos sumaban 3 dólares a un pico de jornada de 101,02 dólares y un máximo desde el 21 de septiembre. En lo que va de semana, el Brent ha subido alrededor de un 4% y el WTI un 8,5%. "El conflicto en Oriente Medio sigue reapareciendo y creo que es cuestionable la cantidad de gasóleo que Rusia puede suministrar realmente a los mercados. Esos dos factores siguen impulsando a los operadores a comprar", afirmó Dennis Kissler, vicepresidente sénior de operaciones de BOK Financial. * La inquietud por el suministro también aumentó al recrudecer los ataques en torno al estrecho de Ormuz durante los últimos 10 días, y con Irán afirmando que está intensificando los ataques en respuesta al bloqueo estadounidense de sus puertos y a las sanciones más duras introducidas el mes pasado. * Los hutíes lanzaron el jueves misiles contra el complejo del palacio presidencial de Yemen, en la ciudad sureña de Adén, matando a dos guardias, mientras que la coalición liderada por Arabia Saudita en Yemen detalló decenas de ataques contra infraestructuras saudíes en el marco de este conflicto cada vez más intenso. "La intensificación de los ataques iraníes provocó una fuerte caída de los flujos de crudo del Golfo", dijeron analistas de Kpler en un reporte el jueves, añadiendo que esperan una recuperación más lenta y desigual de los flujos por el estrecho de Ormuz a falta de un acuerdo político global. Mientras tanto, Ucrania atacó el jueves una refinería de petróleo rusa después de que el presidente Volodimir Zelenski declarara que Kiev abandonaba el alto el fuego sobre las instalaciones energéticas anunciado por el presidente Donald Trump y criticara la disposición de este último a llegar a acuerdos con Moscú. La refinería de petróleo rusa de Riazán ha suspendido las operaciones en una unidad de destilación primaria de crudo tras un ataque con drones en la región el jueves, informaron dos fuentes del sector a Reuters. La AIE acordó el jueves liberar más de 20 millones de barriles de combustible al mercado.

item.title: CoreWeave stock, bond set for weekly plunge as rate-hike fears hit AI bet
item.description: CoreWeave's shares and bond were set for steep weekly losses on Friday, underscoring investor worries over the cloud-computing company's $50 billion debt load that has rippled across the AI industry.
item.dc:creator: Shashwat Chauhan, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) shares and bond were set for steep weekly losses on Friday, underscoring investor worries over the cloud-computing company's $50 billion debt load that has rippled across the AI industry. The Nvidia-backed company came into focus this week after the latest inflation data boosted bets on [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"interest-rate hikes"], raising the chances of higher payout on borrowings by data center and AI infrastructure firms with huge debt. CoreWeave shares fell more than 11% on Friday, taking their weekly losses to nearly 25%. If the current levels hold, they are set for their worst week in over 11 months. "Its not just CoreWeave, there's several (companies) that are falling into this category because of concerns that the revenue is just not going to be there to turn a profit and maintain the amount of debt that these companies are taking on," said Todd Schoenberger, chief investment officer at CrossCheck Management. Investor worries over CoreWeave's massive debt load had a contagion affect that impacted rival Nebius Group (NBIS.O) , whose shares were set for their steepest weekly fall in two months. Nebius (NBIS.O) dropped 10% and data center operators Applied Digital (APLD.O) and IREN (IREN.O) slipped 9% each. The selloff is a stark reminder that AI companies' reliance on debt is becoming a risk for investors and punctures the notion that companies at the heart of the AI boom are immune to macroeconomic headwinds. CoreWeave's stock has already lost about a fifth of its value, or nearly 9.6 billion, so far this month. The steepest decline this week came on Wednesday, when the stock dropped 15.5%. Short sellers made around $806 million, the fourth best single day for CoreWeave shorts since the stock listed in March 2025, according to data analytics firm ORTEX. DEBT MARKET JITTERS The yield on CoreWeave's October 2031 maturity dollar bond briefly surged past 16% on Thursday. It is set to decline for a fifth straight week, down about 3 cents on the dollar this week. The cost of insuring against CoreWeave's debt has surged past 1,000 basis points to record highs this week, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence. Still, several analysts were not ready to throw in the towel. Evercore analysts maintained their outperform rating on CoreWeave stock. "The markets appear to be extrapolating a higher secondary-market bond yield as evidence the business model has stopped working, which we don't think is the case," they wrote in a note. Given the circular nature of AI financing and Nvidia's stake in CoreWeave, Brian Reynolds, chief market strategist at Reynolds Strategy, said Nvidia could also offer buy it. "At a small premium to the current stock price, but far below where the stock had been trading in the past," he said. "We understand that this may not be a likely option, but... it may not be far-fetched." Nvidia is CoreWeave's second-largest investor and its CEO Jensen Huang recently gave the cloud company [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"a vote of confidence"], saying its financial strength was "improving every day". But his endorsement is yet to lift CoreWeave's stock, a contrast from June when his support for Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) [USN:L4N42A0MP TEXT:"sent shares soaring"]. Other analysts argued the rout in CoreWeave should not be seen as a sign that the AI rally is coming to an end. "You cannot take CoreWeave as the poster child for AI," said Tommaso Leodari, chief investment officer at Dubai-based hedge fund Index & Cie. Exchange traded funds managed by Cathie Wood's ARK Invest have been lapping up CoreWeave shares over the last two sessions, with total purchases exceeding 381,000 shares. Retail investors have also bought into the weakness, buying up net $66 million worth of the stock so far this week, which is the second highest weekly figure on record, according to Vanda data. Separately, regulatory filings showed CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator and entities linked to him have [USN:L6N4620WG TEXT:"sold nearly $1 billion"] of stock, mostly under prearranged trading plans, since the company's IPO in March 2025,

item.title: Blue Origin targets multiple New Glenn launches weekly by end of decade
item.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 16 : Blue Origin is targeting multiple flights per week of its New Glenn rocket by the end of the decade, a company executive said on Friday, as it spends billions of dollars on infrastructure needed to match rival SpaceX's launch dominance.Jeff Bezos' space firm also plans to add more launch

Blue Origin targets multiple New Glenn launches weekly by end of decade

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 16 : Blue Origin is targeting multiple flights per week of its New Glenn rocket by the end of the decade, a company executive said on Friday, as it spends billions of dollars on infrastructure needed to match rival SpaceX's launch dominance. Jeff Bezos' space firm also plans to add more launch and landing pads in Florida for New Glenn, its flagship heavy-lift orbital rocket that has been grounded for the year since exploding on the company's only launchpad in May. Blue Origin has invested over $3 billion to date in its sprawling Florida production and rocket integration facilities that span roughly 31 acres with some 5,000 employees, Ian Richardson, senior vice president of operations, said in a company blog post. A $330 million expansion to those facilities will support production of a heavier-lift version of the rocket, New Glenn 9x4, and is targeted for completion in the summer of 2027, Richardson said, adding it will allow annual production of up to 150 upper stages of the rocket.

"These investments are centered on one goal: building the capacity to support more missions, more reliably, and more efficiently," Richardson said. "As we look ahead, this infrastructure is designed to support multiple flights per week by the end of the decade." The New Glenn explosion in May, which happened days before a planned launch of Amazon satellites, badly damaged the company's Florida launchpad, where the 30-storey-tall (322 feet) rocket had lifted off three times since its 2025 debut. New Glenn is expected to return to flight early next year. Its last flight, in April, was its first mission failure when an issue with the rocket's second stage put a satellite from its customer AST SpaceMobile into the wrong orbit, causing it to fall back into Earth's atmosphere. Blue Origin is one of the main launch providers for Amazon's budding satellite internet constellation, Leo, which will rival SpaceX's Starlink. New Glenn's explosion upended Amazon's launch schedule with the rocket, tightening a global launch squeeze that has left dozens of satellite companies desperate for rides to space. Blue Origin has been pressed to return the rocket to its pad, with CEO Dave Limp seeing it as the company's top priority among an array of other programs, including a multibillion-dollar NASA assignment to build a lunar lander that will return astronauts to the moon. Elon Musk's SpaceX, the world's most active launch provider, had 165 Falcon missions last year, mostly carrying its in-house Starlink satellites. Musk envisions launching hundreds of missions per year with Starship, the company's next-generation rocket.

Source: Reuters

item.title: ＥＣＢ、年内に少なくともあと1回0.25％利上げ ＩＭＦ予想
item.description: [バンコク １６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１６日公表した欧州経済の定期見通し報告書で、欧州中央銀行...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＥＣＢ、年内に少なくともあと1回0.25％利上げ　ＩＭＦ予想 10/16 19:03 配信

IMFのロゴ。2024年11月にワシントンで撮影。REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

[バンコク １６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１６日公表した欧州経済の定期見通し報告書で、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が高インフレを抑えるため、年内に少なくともあと１回、２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の利上げを実施する可能性が高いとの見方を示した。

米国とイスラエルの対イラン攻撃を背景にエネルギー価格が急騰しインフレが加速したことを受けて、ＥＣＢは６月と９月にそれぞれ２５ｂｐの利上げを実施した。

ＩＭＦは「われわれの分析では、コアインフレを十分に抑制し続けるには、２０２６年中に少なくともあと１回、２５ｂｐの政策金利引き上げが必要になる」と指摘。「２６年より先の政策は今後のデータに応じて調整すべきだが、２８年にインフレ率を確実に目標へ回帰させるには、さらなる引き締めが必要になる可能性が高い」とした。

また「エネルギー価格上昇の影響を和らげるための財政支援は、慎重に設計しなければ、インフレ抑制の取り組みを損なう恐れがある」とも指摘した。

item.title: As AI rally wobbles, stock market's spotlight turns to earnings
item.description: NEW YORK, Oct 16 : Stumbles in the market-leading AI trade are set to test investor confidence in the rally in the coming week as Wall Street focuses on quarterly results due from key players including Meta Platforms.AI-linked stocks, central to the bull market that just marked its four-year anniversary, str

As AI rally wobbles, stock market's spotlight turns to earnings

FILE PHOTO: "AI Artificial Intelligence" words, a keyboard and a robotics hand in this illustration taken, September 23, 2026. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 16 : Stumbles in the market-leading AI trade are set to test investor confidence in the rally in the coming week as Wall Street focuses on quarterly results due from key players including Meta Platforms. AI-linked stocks, central to the bull market that just marked its four-year anniversary, struggled in recent days, with sharp declines in shares of semiconductor companies and tech hardware firms such as Dell Technologies. Meta, among the hyperscalers spending massively to build AI data centers, highlights the upcoming week of quarterly reports, along with semiconductor firms Lam Research and Texas Instruments. "It certainly feels like the narrative in the market is a little bit jittery," said Garrett Melson, portfolio strategist with Natixis Investment Managers Solutions. "Clearly there's a lot of uncertainty around where AI stands right now."

Worries rippled through markets over risks tied to the financing of the AI build-out boom, which has lifted profits for a wide swath of companies and boosted economic growth. Investors were watching developments with CoreWeave, an AI cloud company with about $50 billion in debt. This week, its shares tumbled. In other recent signs of caution, strategists at Deutsche Bank and RBC Capital Markets separately pulled back on their recommendations of the tech sector. On October 9, Deutsche Bank strategists said the rotation into tech had "run far and the risk-reward no longer looks favorable in the near term." Despite the swoon in heavyweight tech and AI stocks, the S&P 500 remained down only about 1 per cent from its record high set this month. Other sectors, which lagged as tech soared in recent weeks, were now picking up the slack.   "This is very much an on-off switch type of market," Melson said. "When AI is working, it sucks all the oxygen out of the room for the rest of the sectors." META KICKS OFF HYPERSCALER RESULTS US reporting season heats up next week, with investors counting on robust performance. S&P 500 companies are expected to have increased earnings by more than 30 per cent in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES. Massive outlays on AI data centers and infrastructure underpin the profit jump. Meta is one of five AI hyperscalers that combined are expected to increase their capital spending to about $1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs. Investors are eager for signs the companies can show returns on the investments, which would build confidence that the spending is sustainable. "One of the most important takeaways of earnings season is whether or not the profitability of the hyperscalers can grow faster than the pace of their capex," said Kevin Shea, senior equity analyst at BNY Wealth. Meta, whose market capitalization was about $1.9 trillion, has seen its shares climb in recent weeks as it launched its Muse AI assistant. "With the cost of capital going up, this capex blowout is going to become more expensive, which raises the bar for returns," said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services. "Meta is going to be the first up to try to provide some color around that question." SEMIS, TESLA, NETFLIX ALSO ON TAP Chip companies have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the capital spending boom, but the stocks have cooled off. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index has slumped 8 per cent this month, although it remained up more than 60 per cent on the year, compared to a 13 per cent year-to-date gain for the S&P 500.  Investors will look to Wednesday's reports from Lam Research and Texas Instruments for broader indications of demand in the semiconductor industry. Both companies' share prices are up some 60 per cent in 2026. Elsewhere, investors will focus on results from Elon Musk's Tesla, another signature stock of the tech bull market. Streaming giant Netflix, consumer products company Procter & Gamble and engine maker GE Aerospace are among other high-profile reports in the coming week. The rise in Treasury yields and prospects for further rate hikes from the Federal Reserve also remain front-burner issues for stock investors. Hot inflation data this week boosted bets on another rate increase at the Fed's meeting at the end of October. Futures pricing suggested most investors still expect the US central bank to wait until its meeting in December to raise rates for a second time this year. "Another strong earnings season should help equities withstand moderately higher rates," analysts at UBS Global Wealth Management said in a note on Thursday.

Source: Reuters
